parsed.headline: Civic organizations provide resources for upcoming Toronto municipal election

pages.text: With Toronto's municipal election just over two weeks away, various civic organizations are offering resources to inform voters. The election features more than 50 candidates running for mayor and multiple councillors in each ward, with platforms addressing issues such as housing, transit affordability, and public safety. According to CBC Toronto, these resources aim to assist residents in navigating the candidate field before election day.  The Toronto Public Library (TPL) has launched a citywide initiative called Celebrate Democracy to help residents learn about the democratic process and the candidates. A central component of this initiative is KnowYourVote.to, an interactive website designed for residents to find candidates in their specific wards and compare positions on key issues like housing and public safety. Nan Davies, TPL's manager of learning and community engagement, stated the initiative is intended to help people feel more connected to the city and democracy, noting that the library provides unbiased, free, and neutral information. The library's programming includes events focused on voter engagement, misinformation, and trust in institutions. These efforts are designed for all ages, including specific elements for children and teens, as well as an election information campaign on TikTok aimed at younger voters who consume news via social media.

parsed.headline: UK-Ghana Trade Resource Centre launched at 2026 investment summit

pages.text: The UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC), in partnership with the UK-Ghana Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET) Programme, has launched the UK-Ghana Trade Resource Centre. The launch was a major outcome of the UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit 2026, a three-day event involving government leaders, investors, and business executives under the theme, “A Decade of Trust, A Future Always On: Scaling the UK-Ghana Growth Partnership.” The Centre is designed as a market-access platform to help businesses identify opportunities, navigate export requirements, and build commercial partnerships between Ghana and the United Kingdom. Total bilateral trade between the two nations reached approximately £1.6 billion in the year to Q1 2026, though officials noted significant untapped opportunities remain for businesses in both countries. Adjoba Kyiamah, the Executive Director of the UKGCC, stated the Centre is a step toward addressing information and market-access challenges for businesses seeking to trade between the two nations. The platform aims to support firms in taking advantage of the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement (TPA) by providing guidance, market intelligence, and trade facilitation services.

The Trade Resource Centre will provide specific services for different business types. For export-ready Ghanaian businesses, the Centre is intended to offer market-specific guidance, export readiness support, referrals to technical expertise, and connections to British buyers and commercial networks. It will also work with partners to identify firms and facilitate business matchmaking. For importers and UK businesses looking to source from Ghana, the Centre will provide access to industry networks, partner referrals, and commercial linkage support to improve trade flows. The Centre has been established as a core UKGCC function to help businesses navigate the bilateral trade landscape and maximize opportunities under the UK-Ghana TPA.

parsed.headline: Trump asks US Supreme Court to revive dismissed lawsuit against Hillary Clinton

pages.text: On October 9, 2026, President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court to revive a dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival, Hillary Clinton. According to Arab News, Trump is accusing Clinton, former FBI Director James Comey, and others of conspiring to rig the 2016 election by linking his campaign to Russia. The lawsuit, which alleges racketeering and a conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood, was originally filed in a Florida federal court in 2022 while Trump was out of office. In the complaint, Trump alleged that Clinton and her allies used a “false narrative” regarding collusion with Russia to discredit his campaign. The legal action names several other defendants, including former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele and the Democratic National Committee.

The appeal follows a dismissal by US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks, who cited numerous inadequacies in the suit, including that Trump waited too long to bring certain claims. Judge Middlebrooks also imposed nearly $1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers, characterizing the suit as “frivolous.” A US appeals court subsequently upheld both the dismissal and the sanctions. While US government officials and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between the Trump campaign and Russian operatives seeking to influence the 2016 election, Trump has characterized the idea of Russian interference as a “hoax.”

parsed.headline: Bangladesh among finalists for 2026 AI for Climate Action Award

pages.text: Five AI-powered climate solutions from Bangladesh, Indonesia, Tanzania, and Mali have been selected as finalists for the 2026 AI for Climate Action Award, according to The Financial Express Bangladesh. The award is hosted by the UN Climate Change Technology Mechanism in partnership with the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA). The program recognizes locally driven artificial intelligence applications designed to support climate change mitigation and adaptation in small island developing States (SIDS) and least developed countries (LDCs). The finalists are scheduled to showcase their innovations at the AI for Climate Action Forum 2026 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, on 13–14 October, where the winner will be announced.
